subject: Clarify: Pricing exhibit smoothing + packaging carveout — proposed wording
messages:
From: Acme Legal <contracts@acmehealth.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pricing exhibit — caps/floors language and packaging question

Hi Camila,

Attached are Acme’s redlines to the Order Form and Pricing Exhibit (see attachment: Acme_OrderForm_v3.pdf). Two quick points we’d like you to review:

1) Exhibit B (Pricing) — Section 2 (Minimum Fee Guardrail): Acme’s counsel added a one-year floor carveout for pilot engagements and M&A transitions. The language we suggested limits the floor to “Commercial Production” and excludes the first 12 months of an initial pilot or divestiture period.

2) Packaging definition — we’ve flagged ambiguity around how seat-based bundles vs. token/package bundles are treated for true-up calculations. If packaging is treated as a combinable SKU, we need confirmation that volume calculations will be based on token-equivalent or the SKU list price.

We can iterate quickly — copying Oliver (procurement) and Nina (legal). Are you able to provide a counterproposal on the pilot carveout and a short explanation of how you intend to compute packaging true-ups?

Thanks,
Nina Park
Senior Counsel, Acme Health
contracts@acmehealth.com

---
Attachment: Acme_OrderForm_v3.pdf (605 KB, redline PDF stub)
From: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
To: Nina Park <contracts@acmehealth.com>, Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — caps/floors language and packaging question

Nina — thanks for the redlines and clear flags. Quick answers up-front, then proposed next steps below.

- Pilot carveout: Redwood’s position is that commercial minimums are designed to protect committed capacity and pricing stability. We’re open to a limited carveout for an initial pilot but need to preserve the spirit of the minimum beyond unreasonable opt-outs. Proposed: allow a one-time 3-month pilot carveout (not 12 months) for the specific initial deployment, with an explicit definition of “pilot” (<= 5,000 monthly active users OR <= $10k monthly bill) and requirement to convert to commercial production by the end of month 3 or pay the prorated minimum.

- Packaging true-ups: For mixed SKUs (seat bundles + token buckets), we compute true-ups using token-equivalent mapping per SKU. We will provide the token-equivalent table as an appendix to Exhibit B; true-ups use token-equivalent consumption aggregated across SKUs. If you prefer list-price mapping, we can model both and share an example reconciliation.

Next steps: I attached a short suggested edit (pricing-exhibit-suggested-edit.docx) with the 3-month pilot carveout wording and an appendix stub for SKU->token mapping. Marissa, Ben — can you ✅ the legal/finance acceptability of the pilot cap and the token-equivalents?

Camila Reyes
Principal Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0191

---
Attachments: pricing-exhibit-suggested-edit.docx (18 KB)
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — caps/floors language and packaging question

Camila / team —

Quick internal note from pricing/finance: a 12-month carveout materially increases revenue exposure for Redwood if the customer stays below commit. A 3-month pilot carveout is reasonable for new customers; we should add a clause requiring a minimum conversion notice and a rollback to list pricing if they fail to convert. Suggest this sentence after the pilot definition: "If Customer has not executed a commercial purchase order by the end of the Pilot Period, Redwood reserves the right to apply list pricing and to invoice any delta between list pricing and Pilot pricing for the Pilot Period."

Also: for token-equivalent tables, we need to ensure the appendix is non-binding for any SKU created after the effective date; add language that the token mapping is a good-faith estimate and subject to mutual reconciliation on annual true-up.

Happy to review the example reconciliation Camila mentioned before we send back to Acme.

Ben Carter
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
From: Nina Park <contracts@acmehealth.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — caps/floors language and packaging question

Camila / Ben —

Thanks for the quick read. A few clarifications from Acme legal:

1) The purpose of the 12-month carveout in our redline is to account for longer pilot timelines in clinical settings and for divestiture-related transition periods where production cutover is delayed. We understand Redwood’s revenue exposure point. Would a compromise of a 6-month carveout with a graduated floor (months 1–3: 0% of floor; months 4–6: 50% of floor) be acceptable? That reduces the immediate hit but provides Acme runway.

2) For packing/true-up: token-equivalent appendix is fine. We just need the appendix to be sufficiently specific so our procurement team can run an automated reconciliation against usage telemetry. Nina asked for a short sample reconciliation spreadsheet before lawyers sign off.

If you can circulate a draft with the 6-month graduated compromise and the sample reconciliation, we’ll aim to have procurement sign-off quickly.

Best,
Nina
From: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
To: Nina Park <contracts@acmehealth.com>, Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing exhibit — caps/floors language and packaging question

Nina — thanks — appreciate the constructive compromise.

We can accept a 6-month graduated carveout with the following firm boundaries:

- Months 1–3: 0% of the stated Minimum Fee (pilot period, no floor).
- Months 4–6: 50% of the stated Minimum Fee (reduced floor).
- Pilot eligibility: limited to implementations scoped in writing prior to execution and not to exceed the defined usage limits (<= $10k/month or <= 5k MAU) and must include a conversion plan with an expected production date.
- If Customer does not move to commercial production by month 6, the customer will be invoiced the difference between the aggregate fees paid during months 1–6 and the aggregate Minimum Fee for that period (i.e., make-whole), subject to mutually agreed reconciliation.

We will attach the token-equivalent appendix and a sample reconciliation spreadsheet (sample-reconciliation.xlsx) to the next draft. Ben — adding the non-binding language about post-effective SKU mappings as discussed. Marissa / Laura — can legal push the updated exhibit to DocuSign once I drop the appendix?

If Acme confirms acceptance of the above, I’ll circulate a clean exhibit and sample reconc sheet by EOD tomorrow and we can aim to route to DocuSign for signatures mid-week.

Thanks,
Camila

---
Attachments to follow: sample-reconciliation.xlsx (stub), updated_pricing_exhibit_clean.docx (will be attached in next send)
